item.title: AK-Class scenario
item.content:encoded: This SCP pretty closes the definition of an AK-class scenario, as it spreads a behavior (play an instrument), it is apocalyptic as people do die as they prioritize the music over survival. If the affected area increasing by 300 meters per 10 people included refers to the radius or diameter, the area of effect could easily spread to include the entire word if the participation rate is high enough. However, if the 300 meters refers to 300 square meters, it would require over 10 trillion people to include the entire world, which the world population isn't anywhere close to, so it won't be able to spread very large.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
While this is one I like, I do feel that sadly the end of the article has not aged well. By putting the incident that led to the jump to Keter on a specific date in 2016, it dates the article badly as the time between occurrences is simply too short—48 hours. Once every two days. There should be an event in a population center Every Two Days by that standard and that simply seems too high to conceal, much less re-contain. By its nature as an entity that seeks out populated areas and things like sporting events that are often televised, the ability of the foundation to keep it a secret completely breaks suspension of disbelief.
Maybe the last two digits of the year it started becoming active again should be blacked out? Or the time between events lengthened, with them teleporting back to and remaining stationary at their original field between incidents. Idk. but as time goes on, this becomes more and more something that makes no sense, being uncontained by so long.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I enjoyed this SCP, up to the point when I read the log. The log killed it for me. Reason? A "16mm camera" (i.e., film camera) was found, but then the contents of the log consistently refer to video and video artifacts.

The simplest fix would be to change the reference to a portable video camera (they did exist in 1976, though they were expensive, big and bulky 2-part units, separate camera and VCR, and only came in B&W, color was only just introduced in 1976, and as such were generally only used by professionals). To change the log to reflect the attributes of film, certain differences would need to be reflected: First, static is an attribute of video, not film. Second, film reels were bulky. The most common length in use by private individuals would be 50 ft (which runs for 1 minute 24 seconds at the standard 24 frames per second, double that if the camera is set to run at half speed). Larger reels existed, but a personal camera would be unlikely to be able to load a reel larger than 200 ft. So, the log would need to reflect several reels of film being used to account for 20 minutes, with breaks where the film reels were changed.

item.title: It's nitpicking time!
item.content:encoded:
First of all, guards every 15 metres??? Given the exclusion zone is only about 15 m x 33.5 m (assuming the wall lies within the zone and that the zone mirrors the proportions of a regulation US high-school gridiron-football field, i.e. 1:2.25), this would mean one guard at each corner plus one in the middle of each longer side. Given how huge a wall we are talking about, this feels excessive. Moreover, given that even four guards, stationed at the corners, could maintain continuous observation of the whole circumference of the zone, it would hardly be necessary for them to patrol the perimeter.

Next, more on the subject of dimensions. The article states the exclusion zone covers 500 square metres around SCP-332. On the other hand, a regulation US high-school gridiron-football field covers by itself an area of almost 5,500 m^2. I know the school, and thus the football field, are no longer in use - but even so I've found this bothers me.

Another point is keeping low-profile. With nothing to suggest otherwise, it should be assumed that the SCP-332 containment area is located in an inhabited, active town. How exactly does one explain to the local population and authorities that there is now a giant concrete box without roof smack in the middle of of abandoned (BTW it should really be explained why exactly nobody is interested in rebuilding the school after the "fire" or using the land for some other purpose, even though it's been almost 40 years since the incident) school grounds? Heavily guarded, too. Not to mention the fact it's still possible for the locals to see SCP-332 from above, be it from the air or perhaps just by climbing a tree or antenna tower.

Last but not least unless 332 activates every time a fly flies by it really should be specified how loud sounds in the exclusion zone must be to trigger activation. You've already got the Hz (I see no problem with ultrasounds triggering the SCP, by the way. After all, why not?) - so add some dB for good measure!

This feels like it's got potential but IMHO with the bar for quality articles on this Wiki going higher and higher, it still needs work. I'll downvote for now but will happily change my decision if the article shows signs of heading in the right direction.

item.title: Some questions, comments and nitpicks =o)
item.content:encoded:
500 square meter area of exclusion

Not sure what this means. Might be better to describe the exclusion zone in terms of distance from the edge of the football field "50 meter wide zone surrounding the active area" or something.

a 5 meter tall and 1.5 meter thick concrete fence

That sounds more like something you'd call a wall rather than a fence.

all site personnel are to monitor the length and intensity of the sound produced by SCP-332 from soundproofed observation areas

If they're soundproofed, how can they monitor the sound from within them?

30 humanoids

Assuming that we can see them, can you give more detail than just "humanoids"? Are they animated corpses? Planet-of-the-Apes monkey-creatures? Lizardmen?

SCP-332 will also emit sound

What kind of sound? Do they play their instruments? Screech like the pod people in Invasion of the Body Snatchers? Hoot like gorillas?

if a noise between 15 and 80,000 Hz is made

That's a huge range, human hearing tops out around I think 15-20k-ish.

The camera is picked up and pans around the room. Several deceased persons are visible in frame, including the original cameraman

What did they die of? They're still in the room, I'm assuming they didn't get trampled?

I'm not voting atm, it feels like it still needs work to me. I must say that the unidentified person picking up the camera and panning around after everyone in the room is dead freaks me out, in a good way. I'm also pretty sure we've never had an anomolous marching band before, so that's a plus.

item.content:encoded:
"If a subject is able to hear the music played by SCP-322, they will attempt to obtain any instrument near them and join SCP-332 in playing. Subjects affected in this manner (hereafter known as SCP-332-B) will report high amounts of anxiety if unable to obtain a musical instrument within 10 minutes of coming under SCP-332's effect. If they are unable to join SCP-332 within 10 minutes, they will walk with the band and begin miming an instrument as they march with the band, and will attempt to replicate the sound being produced by SCP-332 with their voice. Instances of SCP-322-B who join with SCP-332 will march and play until they pass out from exhaustion or hunger, at which point they will be trampled by other instances of SCP-332-B and SCP-322. For every ten SCP-322-B instances who join SCP-332, the area of effect will increase by 300 meters. This radius of effect will expand until all instances of SCP-332-B are terminated or incapacitated, at which point SCP-332's active state will immediately cease."

Inconsistent SCP number.
